scenes.heading: YOUR AGENT *CAN'T HEAR*
scenes.sub: Earshot · ears for coding agents · MIT
scenes.say: Your coding agent can see your film, but it cannot hear a single sound in it.

scenes.heading: MEET *EARSHOT*
scenes.say: This is Earshot, an open-source tool that gives AI agents ears.

scenes.heading: HOW IT *LISTENS*
scenes.say: Drop in any sound file. It describes what it hears in plain words, then hands back the moments that matter, with fixes.

scenes.heading: DEVS *NOTICED*
scenes.label: GitHub · first two days
scenes.say: It passed six hundred GitHub stars in its first two days.

scenes.heading: *CLONE AND RUN*
scenes.say: Setup is a clone and a Python install on your own machine. No GPU needed.

scenes.heading: BEFORE YOU *CLONE IT*
cons: First use downloads ~1.4 GB of models
Each quick check loads models first
pros: Your audio never leaves your machine
scenes.say: The honest catch: the first use downloads the listening models, and every quick check loads them first. In return, it is MIT-licensed, runs on CPU, and your audio never leaves your machine.
What should your agent listen to first? Comment Sound and follow for tools like this.

youtube.title: Your Coding Agent Can't Hear. Earshot Fixes That (Free, CPU-Only)
youtube.description:
Earshot is a free MIT tool that gives AI coding agents ears: it describes any sound in plain words, finds the best moments in long recordings, critiques your launch film against professional references, and can even forge new sounds in code — all locally on CPU, via CLI, Python or MCP. 651 GitHub stars in two days. Catches: ~1.4 GB model download on first use and model loading per quick check.
Source: https://github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot
